question: Which of the given layer of the atmosphere has the lowest density?
solution:
The correct answer is **Exosphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Exosphere** is the outermost layer of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It has the **lowest density** of all the atmospheric layers.
 
• Particles in the exosphere are so sparse that they can travel hundreds of kilometers without colliding with one another.
 
• This layer gradually transitions into outer space, making it extremely thin.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Mesosphere
 The mesosphere is the third layer of the atmosphere and is known for being where most meteorites burn up upon entry.
 
 

 Stratosphere
 The stratosphere is the second layer of the atmosphere, containing the ozone layer which absorbs and scatters ultraviolet solar radiation.
 
 

 Ionosphere
 The ionosphere is a part of the thermosphere and is ionized by solar radiation. It plays a crucial role in radio communication.
